MBRDI Climate Tech Student Launchpad Season 2 | T-Hub About Program Program Structure Focus Areas Who Should Apply What's in Store Program Modules Timeline FAQs Climate Tech Incubator Student Launchpad Program Season 2 A program developed in collaboration between Mercedes-Benz Research and Development India (MBRDI)and T-Hub, as part of Sustainability Garage – a Mercedes-Benz Initiative. Up to ₹50,000 grant per team | Mentorship from MBRDI Team and Industry Experts | Prototyping Workshop and Market Lab Access. Apply Now PROGRAM INTRODUCTION Transform Ideas into Climate Tech Prototypes The Climate Tech Incubator program is a joint initiative by Mercedes-Benz Research and Development India (MBRDI) and T-Hub, designed to empower student innovators focused on solving the world's most pressing climate and mobility challenges. We aim to harness bold new ideas to address critical challenges in the battle against climate change. Through a rigorous 12-week acceleration program with mentorship, prototyping workshops, maker lab access, and innovation grants, the Launchpad equips the next generation to lead the charge in building impactful technologies for a greener future. Apply Now What You Get: Real climate problems: Four focus areas: road safety, electric and low-carbon mobility, circular economy, and climate intelligence. Up to ₹50,000 innovation grant: For prototype materials,
Up to ₹50,000 innovation grant: For prototype materials, electronics and components, reimbursed against verified milestones.
MBRDI mentorship: Guidance from the MBRDI team and industry experts across the 12-week program.
Maker lab access: 3D printing, electronics prototyping and rapid fabrication to build a working prototype.
Demo Day: Present your prototype to MBRDI leadership, industry experts and ecosystem stakeholders.
Driving Transformative Impact In Season 1, the Climate Tech Incubator brought together student innovators to build solutions for a more sustainable future.

6 Colleges Engaged via Bootcamps (ideation, solution) 560+ Students Reached 11 Teams Teams Incubated UpTo 50K Prototype Grant 15+ Sector experts MBRDI Mentorship Technical sector expertise Building on this foundation, Season 2 expands to Karnataka and Maharashtra, adds more cities and colleges, and sharpens the focus on taking ideas all the way to working prototypes.
Each bootcamp is an intensive 6-hour session covering climate tech fundamentals, design thinking, problem identification, and ideation.
Selected teams receive structured mentorship, prototyping workshops, maker lab access, innovation grants, and weekly check-ins everything you need to turn a climate tech idea into something real.
Through a combined process of bootcamp submissions and an open Call for Applications, we will shortlist and select a cohort of 18–20 student teams for the Climate Tech Incubator Program.
Focus Areas - Climate Tech Sub-Themes The program focuses on four critical areas of climate technology, each addressing urgent challenges in sustainability, mobility, and environmental resilience.

Sector Focus : The proposed idea must address one of the four Climate Tech sub-themes defined by the program Road Safety & Mobility, Electric & Low-Carbon Mobility, Circular Economy & Sustainable Materials, or Climate Intelligence & Energy Resilience.
Academic Background : Applicants must be students currently enrolled in engineering, environmental science, design, business, or related disciplines at colleges across India.

Build an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform that brings together public data to detect emerging disaster risks, starting with flash floods.
Who should apply ClimateTech, GeoAI, AI/NLP, data-platform, civic-tech, drone and weather or water-IoT startups.

Challenge 02 Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems Precision Crop Health See crop trouble before it spreads.

Use AI with drone, satellite and smartphone images and field sensors to detect crop stress, pests and disease early and guide precise action, so small farmers lose less yield and use less water and chemicals.
Who should apply AgriTech, agri-drone, GeoAI and remote-sensing, computer-vision and farm-IoT startups.
Drone, satellite and phone imaging combined with AI can spot problems days earlier, plot by plot.
Why it matters Smallholders grow most of our food but face rising pest and climate pressure.
Challenge 03 Clean Energy & Circular Economy Zero-Waste Communities Waste is a resource in the wrong place.
Build AI and IoT solutions that segregate waste at source and connect households, waste workers and recyclers, turning everyday household waste and e-waste into value.
Who should apply WasteTech, recycling and e-waste, computer-vision, IoT and marketplace startups.

About T-Hub T-Hub is the world’s largest startup hub, supporting founders from ideation to scale through programs, partnerships, and global access anchoring some of the world’s most significant incubation and innovation initiatives.
It brings together startups, corporates, academic institutions, government bodies, investors, and global markets to support founders from ideation to scale.
Through cohort-based initiatives across sectors, T-Hub enables founders to engage with leading mentors and access structured, stage-appropriate support.
T-Hub plays a distinctive role as an incubator of incubators.
It anchors the AIC T-Hub Foundation, India’s leading Atal Incubation Centres within a national network of 70+ AICs supported by NITI Aayog.

It also anchors India’s largest incubator for the defence open-innovation platform iDEX, hosts MATH India’s leading Centre of Excellence for AI and ML supported by the Department of Science and Technology and is home to India’s first Google for Startups Hub.
Through these efforts, T-Hub strengthens founders to build and scale startups from Telangana for India and the world.
We empower founders with access, resources and allies to build world-class startups from India for the World.
Incorporated in 2015 as a Section 8 not-for-profit, T-Hub pioneered India’s public–private partnership model—bringing together government, corporates, and academia.

Our Inception Incorporated in 2015, T-Hub has provided 2,000+ national and international startups access to superior technology, talent, mentors, customers, corporates, investors and government agencies, among other innovation ecosystem stakeholders.
Coming up from humble beginnings our ideology has nurtured the development of startups at every phase of the journey from ideation, acceleration.
Money Empowering startups through financial backing, offering access to funding opportunities, including venture capital, angel investments, and grants.

As the global manufacturing industry shifts towards Industry 4.0 and governments and consumer services embrace digitisation, the demand for semiconductors is poised to experience a significant surge in the coming decade.

Presently, Indian engineers constitute roughly 20 per cent of the world’s semiconductor design workforce, with over one lakh VLSI Design Engineers working in both global semiconductor companies and domestic design service firms.
To establish the domestic capability to design intellectual property and chips for the future in India, it is crucial to create a vibrant, sustainable, and competitive startup ecosystem.

The Semiconductor Revolution in India The Indian semiconductor market is expected to reach USD 55 I billion by 2026, with a significant portion of this growth, over 60 per cent, being driven by three key industries: smartphones and wearables, automotive components and computing, and data storage.
In India, startups have directed their efforts towards semiconductor chip design, IP design and design services.
Hardware startups, especially in the semiconductor sector, face unique challenges.
They need an environment that nurtures innovation, encourages cutting-edge research and supports semiconductor supply-chain initiatives.
To foster this growth, AIC T-Hub, one of India’s leading innovation hubs, proudly presents the AIC T-Hub Semiconductor Program in collaboration with the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM).

AIC T-Hub’s Semiconductor Program: Fostering Innovation The program is a joint initiative between Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) and T- Hub, aimed at fostering the growth of semiconductor technology in India.
AIM, established by the Government of India, seeks to support greenfield incubation centres that nurture innovative startups.

Here’s a glimpse of the extensive benefits awaiting you: ‍ ‍ Get Free Access to Multi-project Water (MPW) Shuttle: ‍ Take advantage of the free MPW shuttle access for quick prototyping of pre-production semiconductor concepts, validating IP and assessing device performance.

The efficient feedback loop allows innovators to optimise designs and swiftly advance their semiconductor projects. ‍ ‍ Interface with Semiconductor Foundries and Assembly Houses : Use a free interface with semiconductor foundries and assembly houses for manufacturing IC prototypes, facilitating thorough testing and simulation.
